answer: I would like to talk about someone who, quite honestly, stopped me from giving up. A person who encouraged me to achieve an important goal was my elder cousin, at a time when I was preparing for a major exam and had almost lost faith in myself. The goal was to get into a good public university to study business administration, and the admission test was extremely competitive. After a disappointing mock test, I had convinced myself that I was not capable, and I was ready to give up. She refused to let me quit, and her belief in me was genuinely [[unwavering]]. Rather than just offering empty words, she sat with me, helped me plan, and kept me [[accountable]] week after week. She made me a detailed timetable and called every Friday to check my progress. What I appreciated most was that her support was practical, not just emotional. Whenever I felt [[demoralised]], she would remind me how far I had already come. Thanks largely to her, I stayed disciplined and eventually achieved a result I am still proud of, and I got a place on the course I wanted. As for how I felt, I was overjoyed and hugely relieved, but above all grateful. Honestly, I am not sure I would have managed it without her constant encouragement. That experience taught me how much difference one supportive person can make, and I try to be that [[encouraging]] presence for others now, especially the nervous students I work with.

followUps.q: Do you still set goals for yourself?
followUps.answer: Yes, although they are different now. At the moment my main goal is to strengthen my profile so I can study abroad. I find that breaking a goal into small steps makes it feel [[within reach]].

followUps.q: Do you think encouragement is more important than talent?
followUps.answer: In many cases, yes. Plenty of talented people give up because nobody believes in them, while ordinary people achieve a lot with the right support. Ideally, of course, you need both.

note: Made the goal specific (university admission test for BBA), added her practical support (timetable, weekly calls), the outcome and how I felt.
